ambiguities.description: The phrase 'after expenses' does not specify whether the percentage is applied after CAPPED expenses (max $4,000 deducted) or after ACTUAL expenses if they exceed the cap. On a sold-out show with $5,000 in actual expenses, these produce materially different payouts.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net is calculated after actual expenses, capped at $4,000 — artist always benefits from the cap acting as a ceiling.
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable. If actual expenses are $5,000, only $4,000 is deducted, giving the artist ~$850 more on 85% of that difference.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net is calculated after actual expenses regardless of cap, with the cap serving only as a separate contractual limit the venue must stay under.
plausibleReadings.impact: Venue-favorable in the edge case where expenses somehow exceed the cap through dispute or accounting error; creates ambiguity about enforcement mechanism.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: Can you confirm that 'after expenses' means after the lesser of actual expenses or the $4,000 cap — i.e., artist is never charged more than $4,000 in expenses toward the percentage calculation?

ambiguities.description: The bonus threshold is 'gross > $32,000' but it is unspecified whether 'gross' here means face-value ticket revenue only, or total gross including merch, drink minimums, or other ancillary revenue streams.

plausibleReadings.summary: Gross means ticket gross only, the standard industry definition in this context.
plausibleReadings.impact: Neutral to slightly artist-unfavorable if ancillary revenue is excluded and the show falls just short of $32,000 in ticket sales alone.

plausibleReadings.summary: Gross means total event gross including all revenue sources at the venue.
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable; ancillary revenue could push total gross over the $32,000 threshold even when ticket gross alone does not.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: Is the $32,000 gross threshold calculated on ticket revenue only, or does it include other revenue sources such as drink minimums or ancillary event income?

sourceText: Deal: $8,013 vs 85/15 after expenses. Expense cap 4000, hospitality cap 500. +$1,200 if gross > $32,000.
